title: Share GEMI model probes and plane payload handling
goal: Vision: V-6. Reduce repeated model-probe mechanics while preserving lazy prompt validation, endpoint resolution, runtime diagnostics, key admission, inference errors and credential redaction. Share plane-bus string lookup and the two identical deep-generation handlers while preserving defaults and caller capabilities.

reuse.searched: Compared existing four *_ext::probe implementations, engines/http_provider, susi-adapters-llm::inference_wire, core::Provider, key_arbitration and credential redaction; Commercial Apps probe uses are host-contract/admission checks, not a compatible model probe. Protocol body/parsing already shares inference_wire. Reuse the exact existing lifecycle with lazy provider construction; no external source or dependencies.

limitations: Local subtask; parent owns integration/publication and Board coordination. Board check item1647 had no stop/request for CODEX. No external messages, paid providers or production installation.
All behavior checks use fake providers or existing isolated tests; no paid/network provider calls are introduced.
Development verification on Linux only, not a release or full standards-conformance attestation. The whole-core under-100k goal remains open.

results.existing_inline_test_bodies: All four catalog modules and plane_handler test bodies byte-identical to base.
shared_mechanics: Four probe wrappers now use one lazy provider-construction/runtime/admission/inference/redaction helper, preserving distinct runtime context strings.
44 repeated payload string reads use one Value::get/as_str helper; workspace uses existing path helper.
Two deep-generation topics share one branch; ordinary deep requests still ignore model and model-specific topic still defaults to the exact string default.

test_repair: Existing model_rate_arbitration_probe_helpers_admit inspected each old wrapper for literal try_acquire/provider.generate calls. It now requires every wrapper to call shared model_probe::run without a direct generation bypass and checks validation < provider resolution < runtime construction < admission < generation in that helper. New executable regression proves active permit during generation, release after success/error, untrimmed prompt forwarding, redaction and original error mapping. Invalid prompts prove provider construction is never called.
peer_review: Independent review found no behavior differences in SSE line normalization/selection, numeric diagnostics/order, probe validation/admission/error lifetime, or plane defaults. All new helpers counted.
